1.3.2 (51) — MCP Playground and explicit learning-progress links.

Projects → Playground creates a temporary guest Go room or joins an Edit/View link. People and Claude/Codex MCP clients can read shared source, publish revision-checked edits and request Run/Test. Only a person pressing the native local Run/Test button executes code on that device using the existing bundled Go/WASI compiler; other participants receive device-attributed Output for the exact source revision. Opening a link, remote editing, reconnection and AI requests never auto-run code. The relay has no Go compiler, shell or eval.

Rooms normally last one hour and may end earlier on a restart/owner closure. 32 UTF-8 text files, 64 KiB each and 256 KiB total source. Standard-library multi-file examples are the initial Playground execution contract; arbitrary dependency installation remains in the ordinary workspace. Browser participants edit/read Output; browser Go execution is not included. Native runtime limits, including no guaranteed Stop for tight loops, are unchanged. Keep the app foregrounded for live participation.

A shared editor revision conflict preserves your draft. Save an independent project copy before expiry. Leave room keeps local source and last local Output, even after expiry/restart. Local drafts survive normal relaunch; one device-wide session prevents an older in-flight run replacing a newly opened draft. Source highlighting and the existing Go keyboard behavior are reused.

Learn → Share progress explicitly publishes a revocable, unlisted 90-day HTML/JSON snapshot for a teacher or assistant such as Grok. It contains lesson IDs, app-reported compiler marks, interview self-assessments and saved places. No code, drafts, attempt history, names or device identifiers. Reading a shared link does not import it or alter local progress. It is not a backup or an independent skills certificate.

MCP URL: https://gopherforge.app/mcp. Setup/mobile guidance: https://gopherforge.app/guide/mcp. Public tool discovery needs no GopherForge account; every room operation requires the deliberately shared capability. Use Edit/View, not Owner. Mobile connection uses the remote connector supported by the AI client, not a Node process installed on iOS. The relay can read shared source/Output; this preview is not end-to-end encrypted. AI provider terms still apply.

Four coding-agent readings and two interview answers now explain MCP, revision/evidence checks, mobile scope, conflict recovery, shared progress and prompt-injection boundaries. Counts and stable progress IDs remain 220 teaching lessons, 22 challenges, 173 readings, 28 units and 132 interview guides. App Store 1.3.1 (49) was separately approved/released and does not contain the new Playground.

Verification: 14 native model/content checks, including an actual bundled Go run observed by a separate seat without calling its compiler, explicit independent runs, exact draft relaunch, leave/relaunch preservation and progress export without changing learning state. Two native UI checks passed for local Run and the progress preview. 33 web checks passed. Official MCP SDK 1.32.2 connected locally and over public HTTPS, edited a revision, requested Run without execution and rejected a View write. Progress survived process replacement and was revoked. Browser unpublished-edit reload preserved source. Not a full app regression, physical airplane-mode test or real mobile Claude/Codex account certification.
